symbols.name: restoreScroll
symbols.summary:
Links back to a page land where the reader left it, as Back does; browsers open every link at
the top. A link with a #hash still goes to its anchor, and a link to the page on screen or a
form's answer to the top. Positions live in sessionStorage by path and query, kept against the
content at the top of the screen, so blocks that scripts fill above it after the swap do not
move the page. Runs before other `astro:after-swap` listeners, so Lenis, page transitions and
the site's own scripts start from the restored position, and puts the page back on that content
at `astro:page-load` and on the frame after it. Back and Forward get the same correction when
Astro restores the position the page was left at. The first call decides; it returns a
function that turns it off.

    import { restoreScroll } from '@dioramajs/diorama/astro/client'

    restoreScroll('parents')

members.name: followScroll
members.summary:
Keeps GL copies on their elements while the browser scrolls the page ahead of the next frame
(keyboard, scrollbar, native wheel, touch). The created canvas moves with the page on the
compositor until the frame lands, and GL content fixed to the viewport moves with it for that
time. While a `stage.hold` predicate is true (effects: a pinned sticky stage of a scroll
section) the canvas stays fixed to the viewport instead. Vertical page scroll only. Needs CSS

members.name: raise

signatures.summary:
Lifts the canvas above every element of the page, into the browser's top layer, until the
returned Off runs or the phase closes. Calls are counted: the canvas comes down with the last

after it stays above the canvas. Without the Popover API the canvas takes the highest
`z-index` instead, which elements with that same value still beat.

symbols.name: AnimatePolicy
symbols.summary:

- 'input' (default): frames only on input (scroll, pointer, resize, param writes).
- 'hover': also while hovered or hover decays.

  between frames whether a burst in `ctx.overlay` still flies, which an update's answer cannot
  tell before the next frame (a click that starts a burst and hides its element).

  run at full rate.

perspective and focus, and settle into the shape of the text; the crisp text fades in over them

lifts towards the viewer. At rest the element is plain DOM text, except with the hover trigger.

symbols.name: membrane
symbols.summary:
The radius of the round profile over a signed distance field `dist` (CSS px, positive inside,
`cols` by `rows` cells of `cell` px), written d below. The letters are inflated like a membrane under pressure: `u` solves
Poisson's equation, zero on the glyph edge, coarse to fine. Where a stroke of half-width a is
straight, u = d (2a - d) / 2, so the radius u / d + d / 2 is a, and the height
sqrt(d (2a - d)) is a round tube; a dot becomes a dome and a joint bulges. Cells outside get the
radius of the edge next to them.

straight, u = d (2a - d) / 2, so the radius u / d + d / 2 is a, and the height

radius of the edge next to them.

symbols.name: default
symbols.summary:
The heading lies under water: a surface simulated on the GPU bends the letters and the page
beneath, focuses light into dancing caustics on them and reflects the sky, with a tint that
deepens the farther the light goes. The pointer drags ripples and clicks drop them; rain rings
out on its own; ice stays still under frost and cracks until the pointer melts a clear patch.

symbols.name: SHORE
symbols.summary: Ems the water reaches past the glyphs, at least and at most, along its wandering shore.

symbols.name: STEPS
symbols.summary: Simulation steps a second, at most per frame, and drops one step takes.

symbols.name: SWELL
symbols.summary:
The swell under every style: five waves from different directions whose crests focus light
into the net of caustics. Their strength is the share of the focal distance their curvature
reaches, so the net looks the same at any font size.

symbols.name: default
symbols.summary:
The letters of a heading ride a wave: one pulse passes through them when the text comes into
view, on hover or with the scroll, or they float on an endless wave. The DOM text stays as it
is; between pulses it is what shows.

members.name: arrive
members.summary: Pages that change without a link click (Back, Forward, a router call) open through the cover. Default true.

members.name: duration
members.summary: Seconds the cover takes to close, and again to open. Default 0.6.

members.name: ease
members.summary: Easing of each half, from 0..1 to 0..1. Default cubic in-out.

members.name: links
members.summary:
Hold link clicks while the cover closes, then pass them on to the router. Routers that wait
by themselves (Astro ClientRouter) are not held. Default true.

members.name: wait

Seconds the closed cover waits, at most, for the new page's first screen (its pictures and
models) before it opens. Default 0.5.
